findings.text: Host bringup for the Intel backend validates processor virtualization support, prepares enlightened and native control descriptors, initializes shared vendor state, selects side channel flush behavior, prepares per CPU tracking and posted wakeup state, and finally validates nested image layout. Early descriptor or vendor failures abort with an error, while flush selection failure releases vendor state before returning.
Per CPU posted wakeup preparation creates an empty list of virtual CPUs awaiting notification on that CPU and initializes the associated wakeup protection primitive.
The wakeup list and its protection primitive are colocated per CPU and initialized together during early CPU setup, establishing that both are ready before scheduling use.

Enlightened handling and hardware control parsing complete before shared vendor bringup so capability results are visible to later stages, and flush selection runs after shared bringup because it depends on paging mode enablement. Per CPU list preparation and nested offset validation occur only after successful vendor and flush setup.

Mitigation choice starts with fast paths that record no flush needed when the flaw is absent, when paging extensions are disabled, or when hardware advertises avoidance. An automatic request is then resolved through global policy into never, conditional, or always, with a forced full policy overriding to always. Any active choice arms a global flush indicator and arms a conditional only indicator solely for conditional; never disarms both.

On hosts lacking native flush assistance, selection of an active mode without an existing buffer triggers acquisition of a contiguous region sized as a power of two pages, with each page filled from a distinct byte value to resist deduplication when nested. Failure to acquire returns out of memory without updating the recorded mitigation mode or branch indicators.
Two build configurations exist for flush setup: a full variant forwards a module level preference into the general selector, while a minimal variant directly records never and reports success.

Enlightened interface use requires both an enable flag and host advertisement of recommendation plus sufficient version. When satisfied, the path checks every online CPU for an assist page and disables the feature on any miss; otherwise it announces use and arms a global usage indicator. Advertisement of direct flush additionally redirects the second level flush hook. An alternate build provides a no operation routine.

Configuration begins zeroed, then derives pin, primary, secondary, tertiary, exit and entry controls from hardware allowed masks combined with required and optional sets, while capturing basic, miscellaneous and paging identifier capability descriptors. Missing required support or inconsistent paired controls can fail the whole operation, and enlightened sanitation applies last when active.

Paging and identifier capabilities are validated against their enable controls: reporting without enable support triggers a one time warning and clearing, with mode based execution and violation delivery also cleared alongside paging. Mode based execution further requires advanced exit detail, enclave exiting requires enclave presence, and tertiary controls are used only when primary controls activate them.

Shadow and virtualization features are pruned for consistency: violation delivery to exception is suppressed unless a proving option is enabled, shadow handling is dropped on narrow builds lacking access virtualization, and register virtualization with extended mode and delivery depend on shadow presence. Hosts with defective timers lose timer control, and posted notification requires delivery virtualization.

Entry and exit controls must agree on paired save and restore behavior for performance counters, pattern and extended feature registers, bounds, tracing and CET state. A mismatch warns once, clears both sides of the pair, and optionally fails configuration under strict inconsistency handling.

Certain older processor generations disable performance counter load behavior on both entry and exit because exit could mishandle upper counter bits, falling back to explicit register handling with a one time notice.

The hardware basic descriptor must describe a control region fitting within a single page, using a mandated caching attribute for control memory; wide builds additionally reject descriptors that limit physical addresses to narrow width.

Thirty two bit adjustment combines desired controls with hardware must zero and must one masks and rejects when any required bit is unsupported. Sixty four bit adjustment intersects desired tertiary controls with hardware allowance without a required set.
Defective timer detection normalizes identification by clearing reserved bit ranges before table lookup, while enclave detection requires both sufficient maximum leaf and a leaf feature bit.
Each control group is masked against its enlightened supported set; any unsupported bits trigger a one time diagnostic naming the group and are cleared before use.

Support determination requires feature advertisement, firmware enablement, and full activation state, evaluated on the current CPU with migration prevented to avoid movement, emitting distinct diagnostics for each failure class.

Compile time layout verification asserts each named member of the nested image resides at its required byte offset, failing the build on drift.

A shadow descriptor pairs a hardware encoding with a byte offset into the nested image, both sixteen bit wide. Separate tables collect read only and read write members from a shared field list using distinct per kind macros that compute offsets.
Identifier invalidation mask combines individual address, single context, global context, and single non global extents; emulated timer rate constant is five.
Nested interception bitmap storage provides two slots distinguishing read versus write, accessed through dedicated aliases; shadow acceleration defaults to enabled.
Diagnostic prefix uses module name, consistency check shorthand aliases the nested entry check flag, and a read only after init flag controls missed check warnings.
Nested emulation success clears carry, parity, adjust, zero, sign and overflow indicators in the guest flag view, then advances past the emulated instruction and returns the advance outcome.
